contents.name: §1.3.1 Line, Surface, and Volume Integrals (printed pp. 24-28)
contents.support: The conventions of line, surface and volume integrals are absorbed into the definitions of the volume and patch test geometries of this page, whose integral theorems the framework cites from the published mathematics items.

contents.name: §1.3.4 The Fundamental Theorem for Divergences (printed pp. 31-34)
contents.support: The divergence theorem on bounded piecewise C1 volume presentations is already supplied as a published mathematical item, which the framework cites rather than re-deriving.

contents.name: §1.3.5 The Fundamental Theorem for Curls (printed pp. 34-37)
contents.support: The classical Stokes theorem for a C2 patch over a finite elementary Green region is already supplied as a published mathematical item.

contents.name: §7.3.1 Electrodynamics Before Maxwell: the divergence-of-curl consistency check on the unamended Ampere law (printed pp. 321-323)
contents.support: The source's divergence-of-curl consistency check is the smooth-branch ingredient of the constraint-propagation theorem; the framework states it as a conditional theorem with its hypotheses and a distributional branch.

contents.name: §7.3.1-§7.3.2 The charging-capacitor paradox and the displacement-current resolution (printed pp. 322-325)
contents.support: The two-surface analysis with a balloon-shaped surface and the displacement-current repair is rebuilt as a self-contained conditional deduction with an explicit smooth realisation from the framework's own definitions.

contents.name: §7.3.2 How Maxwell Fixed Ampere's Law: continuity from the amended Ampere law (printed p. 323)
contents.support: Taking the divergence of the amended Ampere law and using Gauss's law to recover the continuity equation is the source of the smooth-branch computation of the continuity theorem.

contents.name: §7.3.3 Maxwell's Equations: the pair (7.42) and the continuity equation (7.41) (printed pp. 326-328)
contents.support: The differential pair of Maxwell equations is adopted in the framework's postulate, and the equivalence with the integral forms is proved on this page; the textbook display itself is absorbed by the equivalence theorem.

contents.name: §7.3.6 Boundary Conditions (printed pp. 331-333)
contents.support: The pillbox and loop boundary conditions are re-derived as a theorem from the framework's weak Maxwell equations with an explicitly declared stationary-sheet source, rather than being quoted as data at a media interface.

contents.name: §1.1.1 The Conservation Law: local conservation and the continuity equation (printed pp. 3-4)
contents.support: The source's statement that charge cannot simply appear in or vanish from a region is exhibited on the declared switched-charge model, whose continuity defect is computed explicitly.

contents.name: §1.1.1 The Conservation Law: the integral balance dQ/dt = -flux (printed pp. 3-4)
contents.support: The integral reading of continuity is absorbed into the framework's conditional continuity theorem, whose differential and distributional branches are what the page proves.

contents.name: §1.2.1 The Maxwell Equations (1.4)-(1.7) (printed pp. 5-6)
contents.support: The four equations are adopted in the framework's postulate with SI constants; the source's differential display is the input of the differential-integral equivalence proved on this page.

contents.name: §2.1 Gauss' Law, integral form (2.3) (printed p. 8)
contents.support: The divergence-theorem passage from the differential Gauss law to the closed-surface flux identity is absorbed into the forward direction of the equivalence theorem.

contents.name: §3.1 Ampere's law in integral form (3.4) (printed pp. 42-43)
contents.support: The Stokes-theorem passage from the differential Ampere law to the circulation identity, including the right-handed orientation convention, is absorbed into the equivalence theorem.

contents.name: §4.1 Faraday's Law of Induction, integral form (printed pp. 66-68)
contents.support: The Stokes-theorem passage from the differential Faraday law to the circulation identity with the flux time derivative is absorbed into the equivalence theorem.

contents.name: §4.2 One Last Thing: The Displacement Current, §4.2.1 Why Ampere's Law is Not Enough (printed pp. 79-81)
contents.support: The source's two-surface capacitor analysis and the displacement-current repair are rebuilt as a conditional deduction with an explicit smooth realisation and with the framework's own source types.

contents.name: §4.2.1 the amended Ampere law as the consistency condition with continuity (printed p. 80)
contents.support: The divergence computation that turns the amended Ampere law into the continuity equation is absorbed into the distributional and smooth branches of the continuity theorem.

contents.name: §26 The first pair of Maxwell's equations, integral forms (26.3)-(26.4) (printed pp. 66-67)
contents.support: The divergence-theorem and Stokes passages for the first pair are absorbed into the forward direction of the equivalence theorem (Gaussian-unit normalisations re-expressed in SI).

contents.name: §28 The four-dimensional current vector: point charges as delta functions (28.1) (printed pp. 69-70)
contents.support: The source's delta-function representation of point charge and current is the physical motivation for the explicitly paired point-source distributions defined on this page.

contents.name: §29 The equation of continuity, integral and differential forms (printed pp. 71-72)
contents.support: The source's balance argument for continuity, including its verification for a moving point charge, is rebuilt as the compatibility theorem derived from the adopted Maxwell equations.

contents.name: §30 The second pair of Maxwell equations (printed pp. 73-75)
contents.support: The second pair with the displacement term, obtained from the field action, is adopted in SI form in the framework's postulate and consumed by the equivalence theorem.

contents.name: §1.2 Maxwell's Equations in Integral Form (1.2.1)-(1.2.4) (printed p. 8)
contents.support: The integral postulates over surfaces and loops bounded by contours are absorbed into the integral identities of the equivalence theorem, with the framework's own test-geometry and orientation definitions.

contents.name: §2.1 Gauss's Divergence Theorem (printed pp. 17-22)
contents.support: The divergence theorem in operator form is already supplied as a published mathematical item cited by the framework.

contents.name: §2.2 Stokes's Theorem (printed pp. 22-26)
contents.support: Stokes's theorem in integral-operator form is already supplied as a published mathematical item.

contents.name: §4.3 Boundary Conditions-Maxwell's Equations: singularity matching from the differential operators (printed pp. 43-44)
contents.support: The source's singularity-matching viewpoint is exactly the mechanism of the framework's jump theorem, which is however stated as a conditional theorem about explicitly defined sheet sources rather than as an interface convention.

contents.name: §4.3.1 Faraday's Law: n x (E2-E1) = 0 (printed pp. 44-45)
contents.support: The continuity of the tangential electric field across the interface is one of the four jump conclusions of the theorem and is derived there from the weak Faraday equation.

contents.name: §4.3.2 Gauss's Law for Electric Flux: n . (D2-D1) = rho_s (printed pp. 45-46)
contents.support: The normal-component jump proportional to the surface charge is the first jump conclusion of the theorem, derived there from the weak Gauss law.

contents.name: §4.3.3 Ampere's Law: n x (H2-H1) = J_s and the displacement term is regular (printed pp. 46-48)
contents.support: The tangential magnetic jump proportional to the surface current, and the observation that the displacement current contributes no delta, are the third jump conclusion of the theorem.

contents.name: §4.3.4 Gauss's Law for Magnetic Flux: n . (B2-B1) = 0 (printed p. 48)
contents.support: The continuity of the normal magnetic component is the second jump conclusion of the theorem, following there from div B = 0 with no magnetic sheet source.
